paper.title: Analytic reproducibility in articles receiving open data badges at the journal Psychological Science: An observational study

findings.evidence: Text: 'This included two decision errors for which we obtained a statistically significant p-value in contrast to a reported non-significant p-value and one decision error with the opposite pattern' (2 + 1 = 3 decision errors). The authors' data file data_values.csv contains exactly one row with comparisonOutcome == 'DECISION_ERROR' (article 3-10-2014_PS, reported 0.09, obtained 0.02). The other candidate rows are coded EYEBALL_ERROR: 3-10-2014_PS 'p > .9' vs obtained 4.59e-05 and vs 0.194, and 9-5-2014_PS 'ps > .23' vs 0.0165 and vs 0.0138. preprocessing.R relabels EYEBALL_ERROR to DECISION_ERROR only when reportedValue converts to a number, which fails for these threshold strings, so the relabelling never fires. Potential inconsistency, needs verification: the text count (3) and the coded data (1) describe the same quantity (number of decision errors after author involvement).
Claim 'After author involvement, target values were fully reproducible in 15 of 25 articles (60%)' holds in 50% of 16 universes. Single changes that flip it: denominator=reusable.
